events.credibility_reason: Author concedes the main result is essentially Chang (2004) and states intent to withdraw; it contains nothing on Q(N) anyway.

why: All substantive events predate the snapshot. Szemerédi's o(N), Bombieri–Granville–Pintz's N^{2/3+o(1)} and Bombieri–Zannier's N^{3/5+o(1)} are upper bounds on Q(N) that leave the O(√N) claim open: bound, digested through journal publication (Szemerédi's argument via the published restatement by Cilleruelo–Granville). González-Jiménez–Xarles verify both forms for 6 ≤ N ≤ 52 only. That is a finite range of a statement about all N, so it is instances, not a case; this was the close call. The ℓ-th-power and restricted-step papers are variants. Cilleruelo–Granville poses conjectures only, so its scope is none. The two in-window items settle nothing. Hegyvári mentions the conjecture only as motivation. Laishram's talk abstract states no result, so it supports no scope above none. No AI is involved anywhere.
doubts: The Laishram talk (November 2025) advertises results on the Erdős–Rudin problem for a given length, but no written version was found. If those results extend the verified range or move the exponent, this verdict would understate in-window movement. The Hajdu–Papp verification rests on journal publication known only from a search summary.
